name: Lab switch and "needs setup" messages
summary: One Lab switch per app, on by default; Lab features that need a server, a key or the Lab Inbox stay visible and explain themselves in one sentence when tapped.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh install of each app: Lab is on. Upgrading from a build without Lab: Lab is on and a one-time note says so.
With Lab off, every screen, string and flow matches the last non-Lab build (screenshot diff in each app's UI tests).
Tapping a Lab feature whose prerequisite is missing shows exactly one sentence naming the missing piece and where to add it; the control is not greyed out (UI test per needs-setup state).
Turning Lab off never deletes data: queued items still send and history stays.
best_in_class: This is the user's rule (LAB-DECISIONS.md), not a researched product.

name: Honest delivery timeline
summary: Every item shows Queued, On the relay, On your Daylight, In your Reader (or Waiting for a tap), the Daylight's last check-in, and a plain reason plus Retry when it fails.
acceptance_criteria: A link sent while the Lab Inbox is open shows "In your Reader" on the sender within 30 s of "On your Daylight" (mock-relay e2e test in CI, plus one run on Rooted 2).
With the Inbox's Documents set to Ask, a PDF shows "Waiting for a tap on your Daylight"; after the notification is tapped the sender shows "Handed to the Reader" at its next ack check.
The sender shows "Your Daylight checked in N min ago" from the newest ack/hello. With the Daylight off, sends still go out (presence never blocks).
Every failed row has one sentence naming the cause and a Retry button. No row ever says Delivered without an ack listing its id (unit test over the outbox state machine).
Against a non-Lab v1.1 Inbox the rows show Sent / Delivered exactly as today (version-skew suite, F17).
best_in_class: Nobody does all of it. LocalSend (accept/reject, SHA-256 check, Retry since 1.15.4), Tailscale Taildrop (progress counted from bytes the receiver confirmed, "reportedly offline; trying anyway"), Chrome Send-tab-to-self (received and opened timestamps back to the sender). Amazon's email route has none.

evidence.quote: The file shows up in downloads, but there is no notification.
Immich should not claim the upload succeeded when it actually didn't.

name: Big files through the Daylight server
summary: PDFs and books over 9 MB (up to 192 MiB) travel as ordinary encrypted frames hosted on the user's own Cloudflare Worker + R2, with progress and resume.
acceptance_criteria: A 150 MB PDF sent from the Mac through the Worker reaches the Reader with a matching SHA-256 and a visible progress bar.
Killing the network mid-upload and restoring it resumes from the parts the Worker already has (GET /v1/files/{id}).
A test proves the R2 objects decrypt only with the pairing key.
Without the server, tapping a >9 MB file shows the protocol sentence plus "Needs the Daylight server".
best_in_class: reMarkable, Boox and Supernote move big PDFs through their own clouds; Send to Kindle's web/app route claims 200 MB.

evidence.quote: Lost about two hours to a failed copy
I do not want to use the subscription or the RM cloud ... a lot of manual steps (downloading of the paper, resizing using ghostscript, etc.)

what_it_would_take: Deploy the Worker with R2 (server/DESIGN.md section 6), confirm the `ntfy-attach` probe (an external Attach: URL is listed and kept 12 h), and add the hosted-upload client module to each sender. No protocol change.

name: Send the page as you see it, and say when only a link came through
summary: Pages travel as the rendered HTML (paywalled and logged-in pages work); when another app shares only a bare link, the sender says so and offers the full-page route.
acceptance_criteria: [Chrome] A Playwright fixture page that shows text only with a login cookie arrives with that text in the received HTML.
[Chrome, Safari, iPhone] Sent HTML has no `<script>` except JSON-LD, no `on*` attributes and no form values (unit test with a token in a hidden input).
[iPhone] Sharing a URL from Notes shows the "Only the link came through" line with Open in Safari; sharing a page from Safari never shows it.
[Inbox] Every row states "Page as you saw it" or "Link", and TalkBack reads it.
best_in_class: Readwise Reader's extension and iOS Safari share ("the most robust way to save"), Matter ("save behind paywalls"), Instapaper's bookmarklet.

evidence.quote: It handles paywalled articles better than any other extension I've tried.
the most robust way to save

name: Share in place: done in a second, never opens the app
summary: Share > Daylight queues the item and closes within about a second, leaving you in the source app; a 1.5 s Options window allows choices without slowing the default.
acceptance_criteria: [iPhone] From Safari, Notes and Files the share sheet closes no later than 2.5 s after tapping Daylight (1.5 s Options window included), and the host app scrolls immediately afterwards, on iOS 17, 18 and 26.
[iPhone] Sharing a 9 MB PDF from Files keeps the extension under 60 MB peak memory (Instruments) and the item reaches "On the relay" after the extension has closed.
[Android] The share activity finishes within 1 s; the upload completes after the app is swiped away.
Tapping Options inside the window stops the countdown and shows the choices; doing nothing sends with the last-used choices.
best_in_class: Pocket's toast, GoodLinks' Quick Save, Zotero's iOS share extension.

evidence.quote: I mean my point of hoarding is to read it later - seeing the app is unnecessary.
Still very relevant in 2026 — sharing from the Android share sheet still launches the full Karakeep app.

name: Notes come home automatically
summary: Highlights, notes, voice-note transcripts and ink made in the Reader reach the phone and Mac on their own, with stable ids, page anchors and deep links.
acceptance_criteria: A highlight made on the DC-1 appears in the iPhone app within 2 minutes of closing the document, with text, page, note and a working deep link.
Editing or deleting it on the DC-1 updates or removes it on the phone; three syncs in a row create no duplicates; order follows the document.
best_in_class: Kindle Scribe (export to Drive/OneDrive/OneNote), Readwise's exporters, KOReader's highlight exporter, InstaKobo.

evidence.quote: This would make annotations much more valuable as they are no longer isolated to one system.
if we could sync via any of those APIs and sync read/unread/starred status bidirectionally then I'd die a happy man.

what_it_would_take: Reader: a highlight table with stable ids and an export event (broadcast to com.daylight.share with the batch as a content:// URI), Markdown/JSON format with anchors, and a `daylightreader://open?item=&loc=` deep link. Builds on F06's return topic.

name: Send back from the DC-1 to my phone or Mac
summary: On the Daylight, "Send to my phone or Mac" is a share target: an annotated PDF, a flattened PDF, notes as Markdown or a link goes end-to-end encrypted to the paired devices.
acceptance_criteria: On the DC-1, Reader > Share > "Send to my phone or Mac" with a 5 MB annotated PDF: the file appears in the iPhone app's From your Daylight within a minute of opening the app, and its SHA-256 matches.
Notes exported as Markdown arrive as a .md the iPhone can Share and the Mac can open.
An item over 9 MB is refused on the DC-1 with the standard sentence.
Returned file names pass the safe-file-name vectors; a name containing "../" is saved inside the app's folder.
The phone install shows only "Send to Daylight" and the Inbox install only "Send to my phone or Mac" in the share sheet.
The Inbox item shows "Sent" then "Received by <device>"; a non-Lab sender ignores the return topic.
best_in_class: reMarkable (send by email, cloud), Kindle Scribe (notebook export by email), Kobo (notebooks to email or Dropbox).

evidence.quote: a huge shortcoming of the ReMarkable ecosystem
annotation export format is unusable for getting back to the highlighted location in another app

name: Offline-first outbox
summary: Shares made offline are accepted at once, shown as "Waiting for connection", and go out automatically when the network returns; a visible queue with Cancel.
acceptance_criteria: In flight mode, sharing from each app shows "Waiting for connection" (not "Not delivered"); with the network back the item goes within a minute while the app runs, and on iPhone/Android also with the app closed within the OS's background window.
The queue shows waiting items with Cancel and a count.
Twenty links queued offline go out in order without a 429 against the mock relay configured with ntfy.sh's burst limits.
best_in_class: Instapaper ("rock solid for offline reading"), Wallabako (syncs when Wi-Fi turns on); requested and not shipped in Karakeep.

evidence.quote: I was just on a flight and disappointed this wasn't already a thing.
just kind of... spins... and tries to connect

name: Your Daylight in the share sheet's top row
summary: On Android the paired Daylight appears as a Direct Share target next to contacts; one tap sends with no further screen.
acceptance_criteria: [Android 13 and 14] After one send, sharing a link from Chrome shows the Daylight's name in the Direct Share row; tapping it sends with no other screen and the item appears in history.
Unpair removes the shortcut; the shortcut id survives an app update.
best_in_class: Pushbullet (historically); Android's Sharing Shortcuts API is the supported route.

evidence.quote: It'd be nice if I could have the favorites show up directly in the share sheet, and be able to one click share without needing to swap apps and confirm send etc.

name: Automation: Shortcuts, Siri, URL scheme, Android intent, command line
summary: A "Send to Daylight" App Intent that returns the item id and status, a confirmable URL scheme, an Android intent for Tasker, and a CLI with JSON output.
acceptance_criteria: A Shortcut "Send link to Daylight" returns an entity with an id and status "sent"; "Get delivery status" returns "delivered" after the Daylight acks.
The Siri phrase works on a device.
The URL scheme shows the confirmation sheet unless both `quick=1` and the setting are on; a test web page cannot send silently.
`daylight-send https://example.com --json` prints {"id":..., "status":"sent"} and exits 0; with `--wait` it exits 0 when delivered and 2 on timeout.
An empty or unreadable file passed to Send file fails with a sentence and is never sent as 0 bytes.
best_in_class: GoodLinks (Shortcuts, URL scheme with quick=1, CLI and MCP in 4.1), Readwise CLI (`--json`, read-only mode), Taildrop Shortcuts, LocalSend CLI.

evidence.quote: made tailscale on iOS so much more powerful
When adding a URL to Omnivore using Shortcuts; there is no return value.

name: Send as: page, clean article, link or selection, with a thin-content check
summary: A one-row choice in the extension and iPhone share options; a smart default; a warning when the extracted article looks empty or cut short; optional preview.
acceptance_criteria: On Readability's test pages plus ten news fixtures, Clean article keeps at least 90% of the expected body text and drops navigation and footers.
A page with under 150 extracted words shows the thin warning; choosing full page sends the page HTML.
The chosen mode is remembered per site across browser restarts.
Review renders within 1 s for a 1 MB page and the edited title is the title sent.
best_in_class: Obsidian Web Clipper (selection > highlights > template > article), Evernote's clip types, Read on reMarkable (article vs PDF).

evidence.quote: Note in Obsidian is empty at all of our local newspaper articles
best parser and typography I've seen among many read-later apps

name: Send a selection as an excerpt
summary: Selected text goes as a small quote page with its source link and date; text with no link goes as a Markdown note.
acceptance_criteria: Selecting a paragraph and choosing Send selection delivers one item that shows the quote, the source link and the date in the Reader; the full article is not sent.
Text with no URL arrives as a Markdown document the Reader opens.
Excerpt HTML contains only allow-listed tags (unit test) and selections over 50,000 characters are trimmed with a note saying so.
best_in_class: Obsidian Web Clipper (selection wins), Omnivore (highlight from a website), Fabric (share highlighted text).

evidence.quote: Would love to help testing as this is my exact workflow.
share text on phone, open file, copy to clipboard has 200% more steps than share text

name: Note, tags and "read now / quietly / hold" at send time
summary: Optional one-line note, tags and a destination travel inside the encrypted header; the Inbox shows and filters them and can put the note at the top of the article.
acceptance_criteria: A note typed on the iPhone shows on the Inbox row and, for a page, as the first line of the article in the Reader.
Tag chips filter the Inbox list; tags are trimmed; a new tag can be created from the keyboard.
Read now on a PDF opens it in the Reader on arrival with Documents = Ask; Add quietly adds it without opening.
A non-Lab v1.1 Inbox receives the same item normally (version-skew suite).
With no interaction, Quick Send publishes 1.5 s after the tap with the last destination.
best_in_class: Readwise Reader's post-save bar (tags, document note, move to Later/Archive), Instapaper's save banner, Zotero's popup (tag autocomplete and note since June 2025).

evidence.quote: +1 When I save a lot of articles, later retrieval is faster when they are tagged at once.
we should not have to leave the browser to add labels

name: Big files on the same Wi-Fi (direct, no server)
summary: When phone or computer and the DC-1 share a Wi-Fi network, files over 9 MB (up to 192 MiB) go straight to the Inbox as encrypted frames, with progress and resume.
acceptance_criteria: A 120 MB PDF from the Mac to the DC-1 on the same Wi-Fi reaches the Reader with a matching SHA-256 and visible progress, in under 3 minutes on a home network.
Dropping Wi-Fi mid-transfer and restoring it resumes without re-uploading completed parts.
A frame not sealed with the pairing key gets 400 and is not stored; more than 50 bad requests a minute get 429.
On another network the sender shows the sentence within 3 s and does not hang.
The port is closed when Instant delivery is off and the Inbox is not open.
best_in_class: BooxDrop, Supernote Browse & Access, LocalSend, the KOReader LocalSend plugin (PIN, TLS, per-type folders).

evidence.quote: without a cloud service, internet connection, or cable
Lost about two hours to a failed copy

name: Morning stack: one issue with a contents page, never repeating
summary: Items marked for the stack wait on the Inbox and arrive at a chosen time as one EPUB with a contents page; nothing repeats; empty days make nothing.
acceptance_criteria: Three pages and two links sent to the stack before 07:00 arrive as one EPUB with five contents entries at 07:00 (or the first wake after), and none arrives on its own.
No item appears in two stacks, across restarts and sender re-sends of the same id (ledger test).
No stack is made on a day with nothing held.
The EPUB passes epubcheck and its contents links work in the Reader.
Send now builds the stack at once.
best_in_class: Instapaper's Kindle digests ("a personal newspaper with its own contents page"), Readwise Reader's daily/weekly Kindle delivery, Matter's bulk send as one ebook.

evidence.quote: I really love Instapaper and use it a lot. Especially the send to kindle feature
Same feature as with Instapaper. But it would be better if, Omnivore could convert docs to cleaner format and having the option to send either a compilations or a specific doc ... to Kindle.

name: Arrival notification with actions, and Inbox health
summary: Each arrival on the DC-1 can show "From iPhone: <title>" with Open in Reader / Hold / Dismiss; the Inbox shows when it last checked and warns when Instant delivery was stopped.
acceptance_criteria: Every arrival posts one notification (grouped when several) whose three actions work; TalkBack reads the title and source.
Stopping the service from Android's Task Manager shows the warning card on next open and a notification within 15 minutes.
Lab Inbox screens render their final state with animations disabled, and no state is shown by colour alone.
best_in_class: ntfy (priority channels, instant mode), Tailscale 1.104 (tap to open or copy), NearDrop.

evidence.quote: Airdrop on Apple does not need receiving device to be inside an app to receive.
Add a `copy` action on notification

name: Smart intake: unwrap Apple News, AMP, Substack and tracking links
summary: One normaliser, pinned by test vectors in all three languages, turns messy shares into the real article URL and a clean title.
acceptance_criteria: At least 40 vectors (Apple News text share, Substack app link, AMP, utm, Facebook redirect, plain URL) pass in JS, Kotlin and Swift.
Sharing from Apple News on an iPhone sends the article URL, not a text note.
A URL whose only change is removed tracking parameters is otherwise byte-identical.
best_in_class: Karakeep fixed the text-blob case in 2025; nobody examined handles the Substack referral overlay well.

evidence.quote: On iOS/iPadOS, sharing to Hoarder from Apple News, saves the headline and link to article as plain text.
resolve the appropriate article URL before the initial crawler fetch

name: Capability hello and version-skew safety
summary: The Lab Inbox announces what it supports in a small encrypted hello; senders enable Inbox-dependent features only when it is there; a CI matrix covers every Lab/non-Lab pairing.
acceptance_criteria: Every sender/Inbox combination in the matrix delivers url, page and file items and gets acks; Lab-only states appear only when both sides are Lab.
A sender that has never seen a hello shows Inbox-dependent features with the "Needs the Lab Inbox" sentence.
Hello frames are small messages (under 3,800 base64 characters) and at most three a day plus one per Lab toggle.
best_in_class: KDE Connect (versioned packet types), LocalSend (protocol version field).

evidence.quote: I can't pair any device.
Fixes older devices being unable to add 1.18.0+ devices as favorites.

name: Opened, reading progress and finished, back on the phone
summary: The phone and Mac show "Opened", "62% read" and "Finished" for items sent to the Daylight, from events the Reader emits.
acceptance_criteria: Opening and finishing an item on the DC-1 updates the phone's row within a minute of the phone's next check; turning the setting off stops all events.
best_in_class: KOReader sync (kosync), Kindle Whispersync, InstaKobo and kobodeck (read status written back), Chrome Send-tab-to-self (opened timestamps).

evidence.quote: I really only want the auto push, so I can spontaneously start reading on my phone
Read your Instapaper articles on Kobo, and sync reading progress and highlights back.

what_it_would_take: Reader: accept an item id extra on SAVE_PAGE/ACTION_SEND and keep it with the saved item; broadcast reading events to com.daylight.share. Inbox: relay them in acks.

name: Email-in address for newsletters and documents
summary: A private, random, revocable address; forwarded mail and newsletters arrive as articles, attachments as documents.
acceptance_criteria: A forwarded newsletter arrives as a readable article and a mailed PDF as a document; the address is random and can be replaced; first use shows the not-end-to-end notice.
best_in_class: Readwise Reader (library@ and feed@ addresses), Instapaper, Matter, Kill the Newsletter.

evidence.quote: It would be nice if you just send an URL to your omnivore email that it would work just like adding an URL from the app.
that would also be really incredible
evidence.source: reader DECISIONS 27 (the user, relayed in research/raw/eink-tablets.md)

what_it_would_take: A domain on Cloudflare DNS, R2, and in practice Workers Paid for reliable parsing (followup-verify: free-plan handlers "may exceed these limits and fail").

name: "On your Daylight": see and steer what waits in the Inbox
summary: The phone and Mac list what is held on the tablet's Inbox (held, in tomorrow's stack, waiting for a tap) and can Send now, move it to the stack or remove it.
acceptance_criteria: An item held on the DC-1 appears on the iPhone within 2 minutes; Send now from the iPhone hands it to the Reader at the Inbox's next poll (seconds with Instant delivery).
Commands are idempotent (a double tap acts once) and Remove asks first and goes to the Inbox trash (F40).
best_in_class: Calibre-Web's Kobo shelves (web decides what is on the device), Readwise Reader locations; no product found that reorders a device's queue from a phone.

evidence.quote: Goes through your inbox one article at a time and says whether each is worth your time
When I read a large article from random ones, and then it's difficult to find it to continue reading.

name: Manage the Reader's reading queue from the phone
summary: Read next, reorder, archive and remove items in the Reader's library from the phone, applied when the tablet next syncs.
acceptance_criteria: "Read next" set on the phone moves the item to the top of the Reader's queue at the next sync; Remove exports highlights first and is undoable for 30 days.
best_in_class: Readwise Reader (new/later/shortlist/archive, scriptable), Endle/readwisereader for KOReader (finish -> archived; archived -> removed from device).

evidence.quote: Articles you mark as finished in KOReader are archived in Reader at the next sync

what_it_would_take: Reader: a queue order field, an archive state, a trash, and a command intent the Inbox may call (signature-protected).

name: Send several tabs or items as one issue
summary: "Send these N tabs" builds one EPUB with a contents page (a chapter per tab) on the sender, with per-tab results and a size estimate.
acceptance_criteria: Ten open tabs become one EPUB with ten chapters and a contents page; a tab that cannot be read (chrome://) is listed as skipped and the rest still arrive.
The size estimate is shown before sending; over 9 MB the user can drop images or split.
The EPUB passes epubcheck.
best_in_class: Matter (bulk send merged into one ebook), TabTome (up to 25 tabs into one EPUB, per-tab results), SingleFile, MarkDownload.

name: PDFs stay PDFs, and "Print to Daylight" from any app
summary: PDFs are never converted; a Mac print-dialog PDF item and an Android print service turn anything printable into a PDF on the Daylight.
acceptance_criteria: [Mac] Print > PDF > Send to Daylight from TextEdit delivers a PDF with the same page count.
[Android] Printing a Chrome page to the Daylight printer delivers a PDF.
Delivered PDFs match the sender's SHA-256.
best_in_class: KindBeamer (Print -> KindBeamer on Android, keep-layout default), Read on reMarkable (print destination).

evidence.quote: PDFs arrive as PDFs unless the user asks for conversion

name: Image diet: self-contained pages tuned for grayscale

acceptance_criteria: A fixture page with 20 lazy WebP images shows all of them in the Reader with the tablet offline after delivery, and the page is at most 6 MB.

best_in_class: kindle-send-chrome (WebP/AVIF to JPEG, 1600 px cap, q 0.75), KindBeamer, TabTome (no-images mode).

acceptance_criteria: With a test Instapaper account, tagging an article "daylight" makes it arrive in the Reader within an hour (or at once with Check now), never twice.

name: Setup coach, test send and diagnostics
summary: A live checklist (share extension on, Safari extension on, notifications, battery, Reader read-later on), a "Send a test article" button, and an activity log with redacted copy.
acceptance_criteria: The test article reaches the Reader from every app and the checklist ticks Delivered and In your Reader.

summary: VoiceOver/TalkBack labels, text up to 200%, spoken delivery changes and non-colour status in every build; Lab adds a one-tap comfort preset and a grayscale preview.
acceptance_criteria: axe-core reports no violations on the web sender and extension popups (CI).

`dumpsys jobscheduler` shows at most one feed job an hour and none off Wi-Fi.
best_in_class: KOReader News Downloader (per-feed limit, full text, images, filter element), Readwise Reader's Feed (suggested feeds from saved pages, OPML), Feeder (per-feed filter rules).

evidence.quote: One of the biggest things that I use is RSS.
Went from 100% to 54% from 7pm to 3:30pm next day

name: Server feeds and digests while the tablet sleeps
summary: The Worker checks feeds hourly and builds a daily digest even when the DC-1 is off, delivered on the server lane.
acceptance_criteria: A feed added in the Mac app delivers new posts while the DC-1 was off overnight; the digest never repeats an item.
best_in_class: KindleEar (1,000+ recipes), Calibre news recipes, Readwise Reader's Feed.

evidence.quote: Your computer needs to be on for this job to run

what_it_would_take: Deploy the Worker (Cloudflare secrets); full-text extraction would need Workers Paid.

name: AI summary, "explain this", ask and translate (Claude)
summary: A 2-3 line summary on arrival, ask-about-this-document and translation, through the user's own Claude key on the Worker.
acceptance_criteria: With the key set, a sent article gets a summary line on the Inbox row; without it, tapping shows the key sentence; a failed AI call never delays delivery.
best_in_class: Readwise Ghostreader (auto-summary and tags, document chat), KindleEar 3.2 (AI summaries, translation).

evidence.quote: low-friction, local, privacy-preserving
A single run could exhaust the subscription's usage window

what_it_would_take: The Worker plus the ANTHROPIC_API_KEY secret (server/DESIGN.md section 9).

name: Notes into Obsidian, a folder or Readwise
summary: Returned Markdown notes and annotated PDFs (F06) are filed into a chosen folder or Obsidian vault, updating one file per document without touching the user's own text.
acceptance_criteria: Returning notes for the same document twice updates one file and keeps text the user added outside the managed region.
File names are sanitised; a Readwise push is not repeated on re-export.
best_in_class: obsidian-kindle-plugin ("later syncs add new highlights without overwriting your edits"), KOBridge (only new highlights on re-export), Readwise's exporters.

evidence.quote: Later syncs add new highlights without overwriting your edits

name: Handwriting to text for returned pages
summary: Pen pages returned from the DC-1 are transcribed on the Mac or iPhone with Apple's on-device recognition and saved beside the image; nothing goes to a cloud.
acceptance_criteria: On a fixture set of handwritten pages the transcript reaches at least 80% word accuracy on the Mac.
A network monitor shows no traffic during recognition; the original file is unchanged.
best_in_class: reMarkable handwriting conversion, Booxidian (Apple Vision), Supersidian.

evidence.quote: Good handwriting support

name: Inbox triage and housekeeping
summary: An optional "hold in the Inbox first" mode with New / Held / Sent to Reader, search, source filter, a 30-day trash with Undo, retention and a storage bar.
acceptance_criteria: In hold mode an arriving item does not reach the Reader until an action is taken.
Delete moves to the trash and Undo restores it; retention never removes an item that was not handed to the Reader.
The storage bar is within 5% of the Inbox directory's size.
best_in_class: Readwise Reader's triage (Inbox -> Later / Archive), GoodLinks 3 (auto-delete read items, keep starred), Karakeep's storage display.

evidence.quote: When I read a large article from random ones, and then it's difficult to find it to continue reading.

name: Android Quick Settings tile and "Send to Daylight" in the text-selection menu
summary: A Quick Settings tile sends the clipboard (and one opens the scanner); PROCESS_TEXT puts "Send to Daylight" in every app's selection menu.
acceptance_criteria: The tile sends the clipboard URL without opening the app on Android 13 and 14 and shows the result as its subtitle.
The add-tile prompt appears once after the first clipboard send and never again after a refusal.
Selecting text in Chrome shows "Send to Daylight" and sends an excerpt.
best_in_class: Note apps (Obsidian, Notesnook) with capture tiles; requested for Karakeep.

evidence.quote: Karakeep #3074 asks for a tile that "saves the current clipboard content in a single tap"

name: iPhone controls and widgets
summary: iOS 18 Control Center / Lock Screen / Action button controls ("Send clipboard", "Scan"), and a widget with the last sends and the Daylight's last check-in.
acceptance_criteria: The controls appear in the Control Center gallery and require unlock from the Lock Screen; the flow never shows a paste alert.
The widget reflects a status change within a minute while the app runs.
best_in_class: Instapaper 10 (home-screen widgets, July 2026); Apple's control and interactive-widget APIs.

evidence.quote: A control allows your app to execute an action, launch your app to a specific view ... from Control Center, the Lock Screen, or by using the Action button.

name: Paper mode for PDFs: crop margins, blank note pages, writing margin
summary: Options to crop white margins, add a blank page after each page, or shrink pages to leave a wide margin for the pen; sent as a copy, original untouched.
acceptance_criteria: A 10-page fixture with "blank page after each" arrives with 20 pages and selectable text.
Crop reduces the white margin (bounding-box test); the sender's original file is unchanged.
best_in_class: paper2remarkable (`-b` blank pages, `-c` crop, `-r` right-align).

evidence.quote: Insert a blank page after each page using the -b switch (useful for note taking!)

name: Send a paper by DOI, arXiv id or PubMed id
summary: Type or paste an identifier; the sender finds the open PDF, names it "Author Year - Title.pdf" and sends it, or sends the landing page with a note when there is none.
acceptance_criteria: Fixtures for an arXiv id, a DOI with an open copy and a DOI without one behave as described; the file name follows the pattern.
A non-PDF response is never sent as a PDF.
best_in_class: paper2remarkable (arXiv, PMC, OpenReview, Semantic Scholar and more).

evidence.quote: Send to Tablet is another issue. No way of automating that like Zotfile did

name: X/Twitter threads as one article
summary: On a post page, "Send thread" collects the author's consecutive posts (with images and quoted posts) into one article, using the user's logged-in page.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture DOM of a 12-post thread produces 12 posts in order with replies by others excluded.
A timeout ends gracefully with the count.
best_in_class: Readwise ("save thread"), kindle-send-chrome's X extractor, Defuddle's X extractor.

evidence.quote: the value of the tweet is the threat [thread], not the first post

name: Guest drop: let someone send to this Daylight once
summary: The Inbox shows a QR for a one-hour guest pairing; a guest sends from any browser via the web sender and every item waits for Approve on the tablet.
acceptance_criteria: A guest sends a PDF from a laptop via the QR; the tablet shows Approve; Decline discards it.
After an hour or Stop, further guest sends are not received; the guest secret cannot read the main pairing's topics.
best_in_class: send2ereader / BookDrop (4-character key and QR from the e-reader's browser), magic-wormhole (single-use codes).

evidence.quote: Download links appear on the device within seconds.
Wormhole codes are single-use and do not need to be memorized

name: Import a reading list
summary: Import Pocket/Instapaper/Omnivore/Raindrop CSV exports, browser bookmarks, a file of URLs or OPML, deduplicated and trickled to the Daylight within relay limits.
acceptance_criteria: A 600-row Pocket CSV sends 50 a day by default with a progress line; duplicates are skipped; a restart resumes.
A seven-day soak against the mock relay with ntfy.sh limits produces no 429.
best_in_class: Readwise Reader's importers (Pocket zip, Instapaper, Matter, OPML converted into views).

evidence.quote: Reader automatically converted my previous folders into views

name: Verified delivery and private items
summary: Both ends show "Verified: size and SHA-256 match"; sends from a private window ask first and travel as private, hidden from Inbox history and notifications.
acceptance_criteria: The hash shown on the sender and the Inbox match for the same item.
An incognito send asks first; the private item's notification has no title and the item leaves Inbox history after hand-off.
best_in_class: RaioPDF's local-only promise; Firefox Send Tab's per-entry private flag.

evidence.quote: Your files never leave your computer
entries is an array of objects holding title, url, and private

name: Pairing fingerprint and safe handling of what arrives
summary: Every app shows the same short fingerprint for a pairing, warns when it changes unexpectedly, and treats every received name and file as untrusted.
acceptance_criteria: The fingerprint vectors pass in JS, Kotlin and Swift and the same words show on every app for one pairing.
Fuzzed file names never escape the receiving app's directory.
best_in_class: Signal-style safety numbers (proposed for PairDrop), LocalSend certificate fingerprints, Warpinator's sandboxed incoming folder.

evidence.quote: You need to trust this URL/server.
explicit acceptance, clear sender identity, notifications

name: iPad: sidebar layout, drag and drop, keyboard
summary: The iPhone app on iPad gets a sidebar/list/detail layout, drag in and out, and keyboard shortcuts.
acceptance_criteria: Dragging a PDF from Files onto the app sends it; Cmd-V on the main screen sends a copied link.
At one-third split width no state label is truncated.
best_in_class: GoodLinks (three-column iPad layout, keyboard shortcuts).

evidence.quote: GoodLinks added a three-column iPad layout, widgets and keyboard shortcuts

name: No lock-in: export, your own relay, a documented protocol
summary: Export history and the pairing, use your own ntfy server, and read the protocol; the apps state plainly what happens if the project stops.
acceptance_criteria: Exports open in a spreadsheet; exporting the pairing requires Face ID, Touch ID or the device passcode.
Switching to a self-hosted ntfy that passes the relay check keeps working end to end.
best_in_class: GoodLinks (no account, iCloud only), self-hostable wallabag/Readeck/Karakeep.

evidence.quote: I loved Pocket. I used it nearly daily.
they gave us so little time to download

name: Reading aids in the Reader: ruler, spacing, fonts, opt-in emphasis
summary: A clear-band reading ruler, line/letter/word spacing, Atkinson Hyperlegible and OpenDyslexic fonts, and an opt-in Bionic-style font, all grayscale-safe.
acceptance_criteria: The ruler follows the pen and finger without losing its place on rotate or resize; no aid relies on colour; Bionic is off by default and one tap from off.
best_in_class: Readest (reading ruler with an explicit e-ink mode, custom fonts), Instapaper 10 (Atkinson Hyperlegible), Thorium.

evidence.quote: it is easy to lose the current line after scrolling or moving the eyes away from the screen. This slows down reading and increases eye strain
the reading ruler is fantastic

what_it_would_take: Reader Labs work by the Mac mini session.

name: Read aloud on the DC-1
summary: Android text-to-speech in the Reader with sentence highlighting, natural pauses, skip rules for footnotes and boilerplate, a queue across articles and resume.
acceptance_criteria: Playing a sent article highlights the spoken sentence, continues to the next queued article and resumes where it stopped.
best_in_class: Matter (HD voices), Instapaper (AI voices), Readest/Thorium (highlighted read-aloud), Feeder (TTS queue).

evidence.quote: the best one I've ever tested in 16 years of writing about apps
Right now every sentence gets read with the same flat pacing

name: LivePaper reading ergonomics: whole-page turns, no motion
summary: Tap or volume-key page turns, no sliding animations, high contrast for sent articles in the Reader.
acceptance_criteria: A sent article can be read start to finish with page turns only, with no animation between pages.
best_in_class: Readwise Reader's E-ink Mode (names Daylight and BOOX; reduce motion, volume-key paging, later tap-to-turn), Kindle.

evidence.quote: feels like doomscrolling rather than reading a book

name: Open where I stopped reading on the phone
summary: The sender records the first visible passage as a text fragment; the Reader opens the article scrolled there with a "you were here" mark.
acceptance_criteria: An article sent mid-way opens in the Reader at the same paragraph; a mismatch opens at the top with no error.
best_in_class: Chrome Send-tab-to-self (page context with scroll position, new in M147).

evidence.quote: Text fragment data used for scroll position restoration

what_it_would_take: Reader: accept an anchor extra on SAVE_PAGE and scroll to it. Sender capture is small and can ship with it.

name: Listen on the phone
summary: Any sent article can be played on the phone with the system voices, in queue order, while the DC-1 stays silent.
acceptance_criteria: A sent article plays from the history row, continues to the next and resumes after interruption; turning Listen off deletes the kept text.
best_in_class: Matter, Instapaper, Omnivore (text stayed visible while playing).

evidence.quote: continuous playback across articles and skipping newsletter boilerplate (HN 2023 request)

name: Zotero plugin: Send to Daylight, annotations back
summary: Items tagged @daylight in Zotero 7 are sent to the DC-1; annotated copies returned through F06 attach to the item, pull-only by default, never deleting anything.
acceptance_criteria: Tagging an item @daylight sends its PDF once; the annotated PDF returned from the DC-1 attaches beside the original; running twice creates no duplicates.
best_in_class: ZotFile (unmaintained, 4,379 stars), zotero-remarkable-sync and zotRm (2026, experimental).

evidence.quote: Send to Tablet is another issue. No way of automating that like Zotfile did

name: Personal webhook for IFTTT, Zapier, Make and n8n
summary: One HTTPS endpoint plus a token on the user's Worker: POST a URL or text and it reaches the Daylight.
acceptance_criteria: A curl POST with the token delivers a link; without it, 401; over the rate limit, 429.
best_in_class: Pocket's IFTTT integration, Readwise's IFTTT feed, Karakeep's API.

evidence.quote: Pocket's TWO BIG features were recommended articles and integration with IFTTT

name: Import from Safari Reading List (Mac)
summary: A one-way, opt-in import of unread Safari Reading List URLs into the send queue, with a preview.
acceptance_criteria: With access granted, unread entries appear in a preview; sending the chosen ones uses the import throttle (F47); nothing in Safari changes.
best_in_class: No product reads it; apps only add to it.

evidence.quote: Whenever I use an item's share sheet to add it to the Safari Reading List, iOS asks if I want to allow NNW to do this

name: Keyboard-first quick send and a command palette
summary: A Mac quick-send panel (Enter sends, Esc closes, digits pick a device) and a Cmd-K palette in the web sender.
acceptance_criteria: The panel opens with the hotkey, Enter sends, Esc closes; the palette works without a mouse and with a screen reader.
best_in_class: KindBeamer, Readwise Reader (Cmd/Ctrl-K).

evidence.quote: Enter sends, Esc clears or closes, digits tick devices

name: Make scans searchable before sending (OCR)
summary: An opt-in on-device OCR text layer for scanned PDFs (Apple Vision, ML Kit), so Reader search and read-aloud work.
acceptance_criteria: A 20-page scan becomes text-searchable in the Reader; Cancel leaves the original to be sent unchanged.
best_in_class: OCRmyPDF, RaioPDF (offline OCR).

evidence.quote: adds an OCR text layer to scanned PDF files, allowing them to be searched or copy-pasted

name: arXiv and HTML papers with readable maths
summary: Send an arXiv link as a reflowable paper with the maths converted to SVG on the sender, because the DC-1's WebView (Chromium 101) does not render MathML.
acceptance_criteria: Three fixture papers arrive with every equation visible in the Reader; a failure sends the PDF instead.
best_in_class: ar5iv / arXiv HTML (no ebook export).

evidence.quote: My dream is to read scientific papers on my kindle, but most of the tools out there render papers very poorly.

name: Warn about fake redactions and hidden metadata before sending
summary: On the Mac, flag black boxes drawn over still-selectable text and offer to strip author and XMP metadata.
acceptance_criteria: A fixture with a fake redaction triggers the warning; a properly redacted file does not.
best_in_class: Free Law Project's X-Ray, pdf-redactor, RaioPDF.

evidence.quote: Manual redact is only putting a layer over the text but if you copy and paste the text is still there

name: On-device summary with Apple Intelligence (no key, no server)
summary: On Apple Intelligence devices, a 2-3 line summary is written before encryption and shown on the Inbox row; skipped elsewhere.
acceptance_criteria: On a supported device the Inbox row shows a summary marked as generated; on others the toggle explains "Needs Apple Intelligence".
best_in_class: Requested for NetNewsWire ("no accounts, no API keys").

evidence.quote: low-friction, local, privacy-preserving

name: Audio edition (server text-to-speech to MP3)
summary: The Worker turns an article into an MP3 with a TTS provider and delivers it to the phone or DC-1.
acceptance_criteria: With a provider key set, an article becomes an MP3 in From your Daylight; without it the sentence names the missing key.
best_in_class: ElevenReader, Speechify, NaturalReader (not researched first-hand).
what_it_would_take: A TTS provider choice and key from the user.

name: Highlight and library sync across devices
summary: Per-record merge of highlights and notes with tombstones, a 90-day trash, and conflicts shown rather than dropped.
acceptance_criteria: Edits on two devices offline merge without loss; a delete is recoverable for 90 days.
best_in_class: syncery.koplugin (three-way merge, tombstones), AnnotationSync (trash bin), highlightsync.

evidence.quote: surfaced for you to resolve, never dropped silently

what_it_would_take: The Reader's library-sync plan (PowerSync, a loose end in the Reader project).

name: Watched folder on the tablet
summary: The Inbox imports new files from a folder the user picks (filled by Syncthing, Drive or USB), deduplicated by hash.
acceptance_criteria: A PDF copied into the watched folder reaches the Reader within the next check, once.
best_in_class: KoboCloud (Dropbox, Drive, Nextcloud), Syncthing on PocketBook, ReadEra watched folders.

evidence.quote: something more generic and multi-platform like Syncthing (or Dropbox)

name: Reading stats
summary: Time read, items finished, pace and streaks, computed locally from Reader events.
acceptance_criteria: Stats match the event log; export as CSV.
best_in_class: KoShelf, KOBridge (local dashboard), ha-koreader sensors.

evidence.quote: keeps a local copy, so you can view it while the Kindle is off
